diagrams.title: Forensic Sources and Order of Volatility
diagrams.subtitle: From memory to storage: the more volatile a source is, the earlier it must be captured.

nodes.label: Memory (RAM)
nodes.detail: Encryption keys, payloads, fileless processes, connections. Lost on power-off and reboot.
nodes.exam: Capture RAM before any isolation or shutdown.

nodes.label: Network state
nodes.detail: Active connections, ARP table, sockets, and process state. Changes within seconds.
nodes.exam: Network isolation can drop connections: capture first.

nodes.label: Caches & buffers
nodes.detail: Data pending write, application caches, logging system buffers.
nodes.exam: This data is not yet in the log files on disk.

nodes.label: Disk & images
nodes.detail: Files, registry, persistent logs. A bit-level image also preserves deleted files and unallocated space.
nodes.exam: System image = working copy; bit-level copy = exact copy.

nodes.label: Backups
nodes.detail: Archives and offline storage. Stable over time, but must be protected against ransomware and tampering.
nodes.exam: An unverified backup is not reliable evidence.

nodes.label: Logs & NetFlow
nodes.detail: Access, authentication, audit, device, endpoint, network logs and metadata. NetFlow shows conversations.
nodes.exam: NetFlow = who talks to whom; packet capture = exact content.

nodes.label: Integrity
nodes.detail: Hash immediately upon collection; record source, timestamp, collector, and every transfer. Details outside the books, §4.8.
nodes.exam: Without a hash and transfer log, evidence loses its value.

nodes.label: Stakeholders
nodes.detail: HR provides human context, finance provides financial records, legal provides legal basis and legal hold.
nodes.exam: A legal hold suspends destruction even if retention is short.
